newsitem.title: FINLAND: TELE FINLAND SAYS SETS FIRST INTEGRATED PHONE - PC.
newsitem.headline: TELE FINLAND SAYS SETS FIRST INTEGRATED PHONE - PC.

text.p: State-run Telecom Finland said in a statement on Wednesday it had launched the world's first service integrating telephones with personal computers and carrying voice over data networks, called Neophone.
"Initially, the service targets medium-sized and large companies which get benefits from usage, services and save costs by using just one network," it said.

The new service is based on Telecom Finland's ATM (Asynchronous Transfer Mode) and intelligent network infrastructure, it said, adding the internet was not yet reliable enough for international voice communication.

Integrating the telephone with the computer would give easy-to-use functions, such as access to very large personal number directories from which phone calls could be made by simply clicking the computer mouse, it said.

Telecom Finland said it would use the Neophone concept to develop future network services which it expected to "offer integrated data, voice, picture and mobile services, exploiting the synergy between these."
